claims.statement: The European Health Data Space creates an EU framework for access, control, exchange, interoperability, and secure reuse of electronic health data, with laboratory results among priority categories scheduled for cross-border exchange.
WHO laboratory quality guidance treats accuracy, reliability, timely reporting, documentation, and information management as essential parts of clinical laboratory operations.

contrary_evidence: Large laboratory chains already operate patient portals and may add trend views themselves.
Many consumers test infrequently, weakening willingness to pay for an annual subscription.

economics.acquisition_route: Prototype on user-provided redacted reports, obtain clinician review through the founder's trusted network, then run an opt-in pilot with one independent laboratory group.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 150000 members at 90 PLN yearly net revenue yield 13.5m PLN ARR; at 25% EBITDA, 4x EBITDA, and 60% founder ownership, equity is about 8.1m PLN in year 5-8, excluding any separate count of retained earnings.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 12-16 hours weekly, with licensed clinicians reviewing boundaries and content on contract.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 72-82% after channel share, hosting, support, and periodic clinical-content review.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: under 20 PLN product and support cost per activated subscriber and zero direct paid-media CAC; laboratory integration pays back after 1500-3000 conversions.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 15-30 PLN per enhanced report or 99-149 PLN annually, with 25-35% paid to the laboratory.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Annual membership is reinforced by every new result; hypothesis is 55-70% year-one renewal among users with at least two tests yearly.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Validated mappings among assays, methods, units, reference ranges, and preparation context improve safe normalization
fingerprint.customer: Consumers receiving repeated preventive or wellbeing blood tests from diagnostic laboratories
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Diagnostic labs present activation inside their existing result-delivery portal after every paid test
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: White-label, non-diagnostic longitudinal results record and clinician handoff subscription
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Consumer pays a report upgrade or annual passport subscription; laboratory retains a disclosed channel share
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A new laboratory report arrives in a format that is hard to compare with prior results or share concisely with a clinician

founder_fit: Directly uses the founder's interest in biomarkers, longevity, and quantified self.
Data harmonization and careful trend modelling match data-science skills.
Laboratory distribution and a clinician reviewer minimize public-facing sales and camera exposure.
risks: Sensitive health data creates high privacy and security obligations.
Generated language can drift into medical-device or medical-advice territory.
Normalization errors can make longitudinal comparisons unsafe.

structure.control_point: Normalized longitudinal assay record carried across repeated testing events
structure.critical_dependency: A laboratory integration that preserves method and reference-range metadata with explicit consent

thesis: Offer diagnostic laboratories a white-label, consent-based results passport that normalizes units and reference ranges, visualizes personal trends, records test-preparation context, and produces a clinician handoff summary. It explicitly avoids diagnosis and treatment recommendations. Labs distribute it immediately after every test, earn a share of a consumer subscription, and improve repeat testing without relying on the founder's personal health brand.
title: Lab-Branded Longitudinal Results Passport
uncertainties: Which non-diagnostic feature creates measurable repeat-testing or retention lift for a lab?
Whether consumers prefer a lab-specific passport or an independent cross-lab record.
How reliably Polish lab exports encode methods, units, and reference ranges?
